subject: Usage threshold rebalancing and billing ladder proposal
messages:
From: Emma Hollis <emma.hollis@clearlakehealth.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@clearlakehealth.com
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal talk — usage thresholds and billing mechanics

Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Procurement asked me to put the ask in writing so we have a single thread for finance to review. High level: ClearLake is planning a mid-year capacity increase tied to a pilot program in two regions. We expect a 35-50% spike in monthly token consumption in months 3-6 of the next contract year.

Requesting: 
- A proposal that smooths cost impact via a billing ladder (tiered unit price that changes by cumulative usage bands) so we avoid a big one-off uplift at month 1.
- A short-term credit or voucher to offset the first-month overage while the pilot ramps.
- Confirmation that co-terming to our company fiscal year (co-term 2027-06-30) is possible without re-pricing the base commit.

Attached is a simple forecast and the pilot rollout cadence. Procurement flagged your typical uplift language about pro-rata invoice adjustments — they asked if we can keep uplift amortized over the quarter.

Can you share an internal proposal/worksheet that shows pricing across 3 bands (baseline, pilot ramp, steady-state) and a recommended voucher size? We need to present to the finance committee by 2026-09-10.

Thanks,
Emma Hollis
Director, Cloud Integrations
ClearLake Health
[Attachment: ClearLake_pilot_forecast.xlsx]

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Emma Hollis <emma.hollis@clearlakehealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-18T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal talk — usage thresholds and billing mechanics

Emma — appreciate the clear ask and timeline. I pulled Ben and Karthik onto this thread to model a few practical approaches. Attached is a draft billing ladder worksheet and a short note on voucher sizing. High-level proposals below so finance can react quickly: 

1) Laddered unit pricing (preferred) — three bands by monthly token run-rate: Baseline (0-5M tokens), Ramp (5M-12M), Steady (12M+). Unit price for Ramp set at baseline + 12%, Steady at baseline + 5% (we assume economies of scale once steady). This smooths the visible per-token increase while limiting overall revenue risk.

2) Time-bound voucher — one-time credit equal to 40% of expected month-1 overage (applies only to tokens above baseline during pilot month). Voucher can be applied as a credit to the month-1 invoice; expires after 90 days.

3) Co-term — we can align billing period to 2027-06-30 without re-pricing the existing annual commitment; any uplift recognized is treated as an addendum with amortization option across the remaining contract months.

Next steps I propose: 
- Ben will run net present value scenarios for each ladder (conservative/mid/aggressive).
- Karthik will confirm how uplift amortization appears on the invoice and whether we can offer monthly amortization versus quarterly.
- I’ll prepare the SOW addendum language and a one-page summary for finance.

See attached: RWI_ClearLake_billing_ladder_v1.xlsx and SOW_2026-08_v2.pdf.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: RWI_ClearLake_billing_ladder_v1.xlsx, SOW_2026-08_v2.pdf]

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, Emma Hollis <emma.hollis@clearlakehealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-25T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal talk — usage thresholds and billing mechanics

Marissa / Emma — ran three ladder scenarios and attached the NPV sheet. Quick summary:
- Conservative ladder: smaller step increases (Ramp +8%, Steady +3%) — lowest short-term bill shock but largest long-term funding gap for us.
- Mid ladder (Marissa's draft): Ramp +12%, Steady +5% — balances risk and incentives.
- Aggressive ladder: Ramp +18%, Steady +8% — protects Redwood but risks pushback.

On voucher sizing: 40% of month-1 overage is reasonable as a one-time concession; if procurement requires a larger offset we can move to a two-month tapered credit (30% / 20%).

On amortization mechanics (Karthik to confirm formally): we can offer monthly amortization across remaining months in the fiscal period. That means uplift dollars are invoiced equally each month rather than in a single charge, and that amortized amount will appear as a separate line item for clarity.

Attachments: NPV_scenarios_ClearLake.xlsx

Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Strategy
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: NPV_scenarios_ClearLake.xlsx]

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: Emma Hollis <emma.hollis@clearlakehealth.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-08T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal talk — usage thresholds and billing mechanics

Emma — follow-up on the invoice treatment: confirmed with billing ops. Two practical options for ClearLake to choose from if you accept the mid ladder: 

A) Monthly amortization: uplift recognized over remaining months to co-term (equal amount on each month). Appears on invoice as "Uplift amortization — ClearLake pilot" with the monthly amortized dollar amount. No change to base-rate lines.

B) Quarterly amortization: same total uplift but amortized per quarter. Slightly simpler for your accounting team and reduces monthly invoice churn.

Voucher mechanics: voucher is issued as a credit memo applied to the first invoice after pilot month. If you prefer the two-month taper (30% then 20%) we can structure two sequential credit memos.

I attached a suggested invoice mock (SOW addendum language included in the PDF) and updated the billing ladder workbook to show amortization line items. If this aligns, Marissa will prepare the formal addendum and we can route DocuSign next week.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: SOW_2026-08_v2.pdf, RWI_ClearLake_billing_ladder_v1.xlsx]
